query: For a multicomponent high-entropy alloy in its high-temperature solid and liquid states, what single intervention could overcome the limited accuracy, availability, and efficiency of determining melting temperature, enthalpy and entropy of fusion, volume change upon melting, and liquid thermodynamic properties across a large compositional space? Formulate one hypothesis that states the intervention and causal mechanism, predicts the outcome relative to current experimental and computational baselines, defines the applicable composition and temperature ranges, identifies supporting prior evidence, and proposes a decisive falsification test against independent reference data.

generation.hypothesis: The single intervention of utilizing machine learning models trained on a dataset of high-entropy alloys' thermodynamic properties, such as melting temperature, enthalpy and entropy of fusion, volume change upon melting, and liquid thermodynamic properties, could overcome the limitations of determining these properties across a large compositional space.
generation.material_initial_state: Multicomponent high-entropy alloy in its high-temperature solid and liquid states
generation.intervention: Utilizing machine learning models trained on a dataset of high-entropy alloys' thermodynamic properties
generation.conditions: Applicable composition range: 3-10 principal elements, temperature range: 500-2000 K
generation.mechanism: The machine learning models learn patterns and relationships in the data, allowing for accurate predictions of thermodynamic properties across a large compositional space
generation.predicted_outcome: Improved accuracy, availability, and efficiency of determining melting temperature, enthalpy and entropy of fusion, volume change upon melting, and liquid thermodynamic properties, with a predicted reduction in error of 20-30% compared to current experimental and computational baselines
generation.baseline: Current experimental and computational methods, such as differential scanning calorimetry and density functional theory
generation.boundary: Limited to high-entropy alloys with 3-10 principal elements and temperatures between 500-2000 K
generation.uncertainty: Uncertainty in the accuracy of the machine learning models, potential overfitting or underfitting of the data, and limited availability of high-quality training data

falsification_experiment.design: Comparison of machine learning model predictions with independent reference data from experimental measurements, such as differential scanning calorimetry and X-ray diffraction
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the machine learning model predictions deviate from the independent reference data by more than 10%, the hypothesis is falsified

cited_evidence.text: The concept of high entropy alloys (HEAs) has allowed the exploration of large composition space of alloys, and is currently one of the most intriguing research topics in the field of materials science [1] – [3] . Recent studies have shown attractive mechanical properties of HEAs at cryogenic temperature [4] and room temperature [5] with excellent combinations of high strength and toughness, indicating their potential as the structural materials. However, the strength of single phase type HEAs were reported to be insufficient at elevated temperatures [6] . Several HEAs, such as CoCrFeNiNb x [7] and CoCrFeNiMo x [8] demonstrated that a moderate increase in tensile strength can be achieved by various precipitates. Abstract The microstructure, temperature-dependent mechanical properties and deformation behaviors of equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi high-entropy alloy (HEA) additively manufactured by selective laser melting (SLM) were investigated. SLM-built HEA had a face-centered cubic (FCC) single-phase random solid solution. In addition, SLM-built HEA was composed of epitaxial growth grains, dislocation network and nano-sized oxides. Room- and high-temperature compression tests confirmed that SLM-built HEA has outstanding mechanical properties in all temperature ranges compared to equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi HEAs reported up to the present. The excellent mechanical properties of SLM-built HEA were achieved with fine grains, high dislocation density and fine precipitates at low temperatures (25 °C to 600 °C), and by high dislocation density and fine precipitates at high temperatures (700 °C or higher). On the other hand, the deformation microstructure showed that slip and deformation twins are the main deformation mechanisms from 25 °C to 600 °C, and slip and partial recrystallization are the main deformation mechanisms above 700 °C. Abstract Developing affordable and light high-temperature materials alternative to Ni-base superalloys has significantly increased the efforts in designing advanced ferritic superalloys. However, currently developed ferritic superalloys still exhibit low high-temperature strengths, which limits their usage. Here we use a CALPHAD-based high-throughput computational method to design light, strong, and low-cost high-entropy alloys for elevated-temperature applications. Through the high-throughput screening, precipitation-strengthened lightweight high-entropy alloys are discovered from thousands of initial compositions, which exhibit enhanced strengths compared to other counterparts at room and elevated temperatures. The experimental and theoretical understanding of both successful and failed cases in their strengthening mechanisms and order-disorder transitions further improves the accuracy of the thermodynamic database of the discovered alloy system.
